subject: Proposal: cadence-smoothing with tiered acceptance to counter close drift
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Close cadence concern and proposed acceptance split

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the team is excited about Redwood but we ran into internal timing friction during our steering committee this morning. Procurement is pushing a single-go-live acceptance window and IT is asking for a phased acceptance approach to reduce risk.

Realistically, the original close date (Dec 10) is tight given parallel integrations and a third-party validation that slipped last week. We're trying to avoid a hard stop because senior leadership wants features to be live for the fiscal quarter.

Can you share a concise proposal for a tiered acceptance plan (what can go live in phase 1 vs phase 2), and any implications for pricing or SLA targets? If we can keep commitments limited and scoped, I think we can keep the overall close in Q4, but we need a documented MAP update to present to the committee on Monday.

Attaching our internal timeline snapshot (not included here).

Best,
Ellen
Director, Strategic Programs
Aurelia Health
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Close cadence concern and proposed acceptance split

Hi Ellen — thanks for the context and the heads-up.

Quick summary of what we'll deliver by Monday: a one-page MAP update that defines a two-phase acceptance (Phase A: core inference + auth/integration tests; Phase B: advanced routing, analytics and canary expansion), an updated risk register, and a suggested SLA cadence tied to each phase.

Highlights / trade-offs:
- Phase A target: Dec 8 — limited to internal pilot, predictable throughput (reserved capacity), and a 99.5% availability SLA.
- Phase B target: Dec 22 — adds workload expansion, cross-region routing, and full analytics retention.
- Pricing: we can keep list pricing but suggest a small, one-time acceptance-split coordination credit to cover engineering hours and a short extension on implementation support (proposed credit = 10% of first-month Dedicated commit).
- MAP change process: we will publish a MAP amendment PDF (Aurelia_MAP_v2.pdf) and update the HubSpot deal record.

I'll attach the draft MAP and a concise risk register (Aurelia_risk_register.xlsx) for your review. Ben and Markus are looped in for capacity and SLA notes.

Next steps: Ellen, if you can confirm the committee's acceptance of the two-phase approach by Monday EOD, we'll finalize the MAP and ship the doc. If procurement wants tighter language on the credit, we can escalate to legal/product for a short exception.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Close cadence concern and proposed acceptance split

Grace — this looks good. The steering committee is amenable to a two-phase acceptance as long as we get the MAP amendment and a short note from Redwood confirming the coordination credit and support extension.

Procurement asked for the credit language to be explicit and timeboxed; can you include a clause that the 10% credit applies to the first full billing month post-Phase A go-live and that the credit is contingent on the Phase A acceptance criteria being met? Also add a one-week window for any post-acceptance remediation (covered under the acceptance support hours).

I'll present this Monday morning; appreciate the fast turnaround.

Ellen
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: ellen.park@aureliahealth.com, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Close cadence concern and proposed acceptance split — escalation/approval request

Ben/Markus — forwarding the thread. Committee is supportive of the two-phase acceptance but procurement needs explicit credit wording and an assurance on the one-week remediation window. They also want us to confirm that Phase A's SLA will be scoped to the pilot traffic levels (we should not commit to global autoscale for Phase A).

Asks: 1) Can Product/Legal accept the 10% coordination credit language as drafted below (credit = 10% of first full billing month post-Phase A, contingent on Phase A acceptance criteria)? 2) Can we lock Phase A SLA to pilot throughput (quantified in the MAP) and note that full autoscale will only be enabled in Phase B? 3) Any material risk to revenue recognition or SLAs that requires exec sign-off?

I've attached the draft MAP+risk register for your review (Aurelia_MAP_v2.pdf, Aurelia_risk_register.xlsx). I'm recommending we accept the credit to keep the close in Q4 and avoid a full rebaseline. If Product/Legal push back, we'll need to escalate to Ops Leadership.

Best,
Grace
